chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far (ibn al-Muzaffar) al-Alawi al-Umari al-Samarqandi (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masood al-Ayashi quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishkeeb, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufy, on the authority of Abi Jamileh Al-Asady, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Khizermi, on the authority of Salma ibn Kohayl who linked it up to Ibn Abbas that he said:

The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Seven [types of people] will be in the Shade of the Throne of God, the Mighty and Exalted, on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade: a just Imam, a young man who grew up in the worship of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man who gave charity with his right hand and concealed it from his left hand, a man who remembered God, the Mighty and Exalted, when he was alone and his eyes flowed with tears from the fear of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man who met his believing brother and said, "I love you for the sake of God, the Mighty and Exalted," a man who left the mosque with the intention of returning to it, and a man whom a beautiful woman invited to herself, but he said, "I fear God, Lord of the Worlds.'"

key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ بِيَمِينِهِ فَأَخْفَاهُ عَنْ ش: Gave charity with right hand and concealed it from left hand (secret charity)
key_terms.رَجُلٌ دَعَتْهُ امْرَأَةٌ ذَاتُ جَمَالٍ: Man invited by a beautiful woman
key_terms.شَابٌّ نَشَأَ فِي عِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ: Young man who grew up in worship of God

ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people who will be in the shade of God's throne on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the interplay between public leadership and private piety, emphasizing that true righteousness encompasses both the just Imam and the individual’s internal state. The inclusion of 'secret charity' and 'private weeping' underscores the Shia emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) in personal devotion, while the reference to the 'just Imam' reflects the centrality of political and spiritual authority in Shia eschatology. These seven categories collectively illustrate a holistic model of faith that balances social responsibility with intimate spiritual connection.
